previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplant was admitted for fevers up to 102.4°F, nausea, fatigue, and mild abdominal pain. He had a PICC line for home micafungin therapy due to prior fungal peritonitis. Workup showed no growth in blood or urine cultures, a negative CMV viral load, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Renal ultrasound revealed resolution of a prior perinephric fluid collection, leading to discontinuation of micafungin. The PICC line was removed, and the patient was treated with vancomycin for presumed line-associated bacteremia. After defervescing, he completed five days of inpatient vancomycin and was discharged on a two-day course of oral linezolid. Potassium remained elevated, so kayexalate was continued twice weekly, and calcium carbonate was held. He was stable on all chronic medications, including tacrolimus and insulin, and was discharged home with follow-up planned in transplant and infectious disease clinics.

___ with DDRT in ___ for ESRD from DM, CAD, ___ (EF40-45%

# RUQ pain, n/v: There was no notable pathology on RUQ U/S and 
CT abdomen. Given n/v started before abdominal pain, 
gastroenteritis possible. Labs were notable only for mild 
elevation of alkaline phosphatase but actually improved from 
prior and no biliary process on imaging. Hematuria on UA but no 
flank pain or suggestion of renal stones on CT. His lipase was 
within normal limits. It was thought that perhaps this could be 
a recurrence of his gastroparesis. He was watched and with 
symptomatic medications his symptoms improved. His cultures for 
stool, CMV all returned negative. 

# ESRD s/p DDRT ___: Had renal transplant ultrasound with 
concern for main renal artery stenosis in 1 transplant and new 
mild hydro in the other. This is not clearly contributing to 
symptoms and creatinine at baselin. Tacrolimus level of 9.1 was 
followed and it wa decided to decrease tacrolimus by half given 
the elevated level. He was continued on MMF. He was continued on 
lamivudine daily for HBV prophylaxis.

# Left foot ulcer: Not clearly superinfected. He had been 
planned for an outpatient debridement; however it was decided he 
would have inpatient debridement given he was in hospital. His 
pain was well controlled after the procedure. Podiatry 
recommended dressing changes and following up on ___ days as an 
outpatient. His path was noted to have GPCs but given his 
clinical status it was decided not to treat him and to follow 
him as an outpatient. 

Chronic Issues:
# IDDM: He was continued on Lantus with SSI  
# HTN: He was continued on coreg, his pressures remained stable 
and he was recommended to restart amlodipine and imdur as an 
outpatient.  
# CAD: He was continued on ASA, coreg  
# Chronic sCHF without exacerbation: He appeared initially 
slightly dry. His lasix was held, but he did well and his lasix 
was restarted at discharge.
# Hypothyroidism: He was continued on levothyroxine 
# GERD: He was continued on PPI

The two right iliac fossa transplant kidneys have normal renal morphology.

There is perinephric fluid collection.

artery shows elevated peak systolic velocity of 262 cm/s.  There is continuous
antegrade diastolic flow of main renal artery. The transplant renal vein is
patent.

The renal transplant #2 (more inferior kidney) measures 9.9 cm.  There is new
mild hydronephrosis, new since ___.  The resistive index of intrarenal
arteries ranges from 0.74 to 0.78 (previously 0.67-0.83), borderline elevated.
The main renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke
and continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity of 171
cm/s. The transplant renal vein is not imaged.

1. Transplanted kidney #1 has elevated main renal artery systolic velocity and
parvus tardus waveform of lower pole intrarenal arteries, concerning for main
renal artery stenosis.

2.  The resistive index of upper pole and mid intrarenal arteries of
